content.text: AGV repair note: record 144027 AGV Repairs - 747130, AGV hospital station having server issues, needs services reset. Preferred vendor Materials Handling System-EMG.
Support chat requested a summary of the prior night hospital issue; UPS reported hospital station issues around 1:30 AM.
Empty totes were reported going to hospital after tip -- given as the explanation of the hospital issue.
Mitchel was called at 2 AM to help fix a hospital issue; issues removing a tote and tipper issues reported. Speaker notes this is second-hand and not well documented.
Andy and Zane explained they removed an AGV without removing the associated tote and basically disabled hospital station; UPS supervisor reportedly admitted doing so and accepted blame.
Case timeline shared in chat: case opened at 2:05am EST.
Work order/service request record for UPS Haslet TX (TXRTH) appears closed/completed.
Chat timeline: CBRE work order entered in CBRE portal at 2:35am EST.
Case 00223554 created, subject 'acb hospital unable to induct', Type Malfunction, Priority 3-Medium initially.
Dispatched P1/emergency work-order record at 1400 Intermodal Parkway, Fort Worth TX 76177.
Salesforce case history: New -> In Progress -> Resolved -> Closed; priority changed 3-Medium -> 2-High: Production seriously impacted.
Case closed (page 16 note).
Chat timeline: original issue resolved at 4:07am EST.
Chat timeline: 5:05am EST - all issues resolved, site running 100%.
Support said they would review call logs to determine when the hotline call actually came in.
A call was requested to discuss escalation path changes because 50% of the tilt tray is now OptiSweep and faster escalation was needed.
Original issue reported resolved; site was now able to add and remove totes; still fixing issues created while totes could not be added/removed correctly.
Site reported all robots were re-added and back up and running.
Support reported no one was on site and they were done with support (in response to a question about who was onsite that night).
Grid-style status screenshot shared in Teams (color-coded, labels unreadable) while surrounding context said the site was reported down and could not start the sort at all or went down mid-sort.
Support chat: Gauri reported the site was down.
Zane was called, was on his way in within 10 minutes, hoped others could assist to get them running.
Site could not start the sort at all or went down in the middle of sort.
Totes could be removed but not added at the hospital area. Same context also describes an AGV location anomaly in the same zone.
Annotated rack/layout screenshot with red arrow; chat states an AGV did not belong in the shown location, two AGVs under the rack in the same zone.
Andy Ackley: the tote-add issue was 'more than likely' caused by an AGV being removed without removing its associated tote.
Annotated screenshot: 'This AGV doesn't belong here, we have two AGVs under the rack in the same zone.' AGV identifiers 1555028 and 1542188 visible.
AGV location/tote association anomaly confirmed: AGV did not belong there, two AGVs under the rack in the same zone.
Garbled page: annotated layout and UI fragments highlighting a position/area of interest.
Annotated facility/layout image highlighting a specific position near the right side, red arrow plus blue circular annotations.
Request to be notified when the system was back up, to relay to Gauri.
Asked whether any AGVs were removed without removing the associated tote; noted that had caused this issue in the past.
Teams chat: 'we started moving' (object being moved not fully visible in OCR).
Teams chat: 'system is running now.'

Summary: two possible issues -- induct tote not working at hospital, and AGV 012 with disconnected tote in system. Hospital was backed up; AGVs 188 and 028 picking up task and under the rack; inducted tote removed via API dog; tote 51 could not be removed from hospital, API dog used to remove it; a few other AGVs taken out to restore. Operators at tippers should pause the station during recovery or everything goes to hospital.

Process covered in training earlier in the year: Aveva hits the same endpoints as API dog; UPS encouraged to use Aveva. An AGV was removed from a zone, a rack was missing an AGV, site used Aveva to add a tote to a station.
Case context: ACB hospital station unable to induct; linked emergency-priority dispatched work order for the same site.
Work-order notes: ACB hospital station server issue, service reset needed.
AGV repair note (144027 AGV Repairs - 747130): AGV hospital station having server issues, needs services reset. Preferred vendor Materials Handling System-EMG.
Original issue resolved, site able to add/remove totes again; still fixing issues from the outage window.
All robots re-added and back up and running.
Closure notice: ACB hospital station issues, inability to induct totes, robot in shut down state. Priority 2-High.
Closed-case resolution details: 'Reset Opti sweep services and had site restart Hospital Lane.'

For the UPS Haslet TX (TXRTH) hospital-station tote-induction condition, use the Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU to pause the station when operators are not present at the tippers, then use Apidog / WCS API to remove the inducted or disconnected tote state and recover affected AGV state. Validate tote add/remove operation on the Hospital HMI / lane UI, confirm affected robots are re-added and operating, and confirm the system is running. The incident did not establish a single definitive root cause or provide exact API request names, parameters, or AGV control names.

structured_payload.title: Recover hospital tote flow using Apidog / WCS API and validate AGV operation
structured_payload.summary: For the UPS Haslet TX (TXRTH) hospital-station tote-induction condition, use the Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU to pause the station when operators are not present at the tippers, then use Apidog / WCS API to remove the inducted or disconnected tote state and recover affected AGV state. Validate tote add/remove operation on the Hospital HMI / lane UI, confirm affected robots are re-added and operating, and confirm the system is running. The incident did not establish a single definitive root cause or provide exact API request names, parameters, or AGV control names.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use for a hospital-station condition where totes cannot be added or inducted, especially when an inducted tote or disconnected tote association is present and Apidog / WCS API recovery actions are identifiable on the live system. Coordinate the recovery with the Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU and validate the result on the Hospital HMI / lane UI.
not_for: Do not use for an undocumented API request, parameter, AGV control, or tote mutation that cannot be identified on the live Apidog / WCS API surface.
Do not treat the AGV/tote association as the confirmed root cause; the incident recorded multiple possible contributing conditions.
Do not use as a physical AGV handling or E-stop procedure; the supplied incident evidence does not define physical handling steps.
Do not continue recovery if tote operations remain unavailable, robots cannot be re-added, or the required Apidog / WCS API action is not identifiable.

roles_and_responsibilities.responsibility: Perform the supported tote and AGV recovery actions on Apidog / WCS API and determine whether the live state supports the next recovery action.
Pause the station on the Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU when operators are not present at the tippers and perform or assist with live tote validation on the Hospital HMI / lane UI.

safety_notes: When operators are not present at the tippers, pause the station on the Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU during recovery so totes do not continue going to the hospital.
Do not perform an API or AGV state change unless the live Apidog / WCS API surface clearly identifies the supported recovery action.
access_or_tools_needed: Affected AGV and tote identifiers from the live incident state

access_required: L2_support access to Apidog / WCS API client and OptiSweep / WCS API
Operator or available site personnel to use the Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU and assist with Hospital HMI / lane UI validation
Affected AGV and tote identifiers from the live system state
system_preconditions: The hospital tote-induction or tote-add condition is observable on the Hospital HMI / lane UI.
The affected inducted tote, disconnected tote association, or AGV state is identifiable on the live Apidog / WCS API surface.

steps.title: Pause the hospital feed at the tippers
steps.purpose: Prevent additional totes from being sent to the hospital while the recovery is performed.
steps.instruction: On the Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU, place the station on pause before recovery when operators are not present at the tippers.
steps.expected_result: The Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU shows the station in a paused state while recovery is in progress.
steps.healthy_condition: The station remains paused and no additional tote flow to the hospital is observed during the recovery actions.
steps.failure_condition: The station is not shown as paused or totes continue going to the hospital while recovery is in progress.

actions.label: Pause station
actions.exact_action: Place the station on pause on the Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU when operators are not present at the tippers.

stop_or_escalate_if: Operators are present at the tippers and the station state cannot be coordinated safely.
The Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU does not identify a pause state.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Operators at the tippers should pause the station during recovery or everything goes to hospital.

steps.title: Remove the inducted tote through Apidog / WCS API
steps.purpose: Clear the inducted-tote condition that is preventing hospital tote flow.
steps.instruction: On the Apidog / WCS API client, identify the inducted tote associated with the hospital flow condition and use the source-supported tote-removal action. Use only the live request or action that is explicitly identifiable; the incident does not provide a request name or parameters.
steps.expected_result: The Apidog / WCS API response or live tote state shows that the identified inducted tote has been removed or is no longer blocking the hospital flow.
steps.healthy_condition: The affected inducted tote is absent from the blocking state on Apidog / WCS API and the hospital tote condition can proceed to validation.
steps.failure_condition: The tote remains in the blocking inducted state, the API action fails, or the required tote-removal action cannot be identified.

actions.label: Remove inducted tote
actions.exact_action: Use the source-supported API dog / Apidog tote-removal action to remove the inducted tote and move the system forward.

stop_or_escalate_if: The required tote-removal action or affected tote is not identifiable on Apidog / WCS API.
The API response does not show a successful removal or the tote remains in the blocking state.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Removed inducted tote with API dog to get the system moving forward.

steps.title: Address the disconnected tote association in Apidog / WCS API
steps.purpose: Clear a disconnected tote association when the affected tote cannot be removed from the hospital normally.
steps.instruction: On the Apidog / WCS API client, inspect the affected AGV and tote association. For the documented tote 51 condition, use the source-supported API action when the tote cannot be removed from the hospital through the normal live operation. Do not infer or invent an API request name.
steps.expected_result: The Apidog / WCS API live state no longer shows the targeted disconnected tote association as blocking the hospital flow, or the API returns the supported removal result.
steps.healthy_condition: The affected tote association is cleared or the tote is shown as removed, with no unresolved disconnected association for the targeted AGV and tote.
steps.failure_condition: Tote 51 or the applicable live tote remains associated as disconnected, cannot be removed, or the supported API action is unavailable.

actions.label: Remove disconnected tote
actions.exact_action: For the documented tote 51 condition, use API dog / Apidog to remove the tote when it cannot be removed from the hospital normally.

stop_or_escalate_if: The affected AGV or tote association cannot be identified on Apidog / WCS API.
The disconnected tote remains after the supported API action.
The live state does not match the documented tote condition and no supported action is identifiable.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: AGV 012 had disconnected tote 51; tote 51 could not be removed from hospital and API dog was used to remove it.

steps.title: Recover affected AGVs through Apidog / WCS API
steps.purpose: Remove affected AGVs from the obstructed or incorrect system state and restore the robot roster needed for hospital flow.
steps.instruction: On Apidog / WCS API, identify the affected AGVs and use only the source-supported AGV recovery action to remove them from the obstructed state or location and re-add them as required by the live system state. The incident identified AGVs 1542188, 1555028, and 1555012, but the current live identifiers must be confirmed before any change.
steps.expected_result: The affected AGVs are no longer shown in the obstructed or incorrect association state on Apidog / WCS API, and the required robots are re-added to the live system roster.
steps.healthy_condition: The affected AGVs appear in the expected live system state and are available for operation without the reported duplicate or misplaced AGV condition.
steps.failure_condition: An AGV remains in the obstructed or incorrect state, cannot be re-added, or the supported AGV recovery action cannot be identified.

actions.label: Recover affected AGVs
actions.exact_action: Use the source-supported AGV recovery action to take affected AGVs out of the obstructed state or location and re-add the robots as required by the live system state.

screens_or_images.what_to_look_at: Annotated HMI-style layout showing the AGV location anomaly and the reported condition of two AGVs under the rack in the same zone.
Annotated facility layout showing the highlighted AGV or zone location involved in the incident.

stop_or_escalate_if: The live AGV identifier or supported recovery action is not identifiable on Apidog / WCS API.
An AGV cannot be re-added after the supported recovery action.
The AGV remains in an unexpected location or duplicate-zone condition.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: An AGV did not belong in the location and two AGVs were under the rack in the same zone.
AGVs 1542188 and 1555028 were identified; a few other AGVs were taken out to get the system back up running.

steps.title: Validate tote add and remove on the Hospital HMI / lane UI
steps.purpose: Confirm that the hospital station's tote workflow has been restored after the API and AGV recovery actions.
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI / lane UI, verify that the hospital station can add a tote and remove a tote again. Have L2 support observe the live result as needed.
steps.expected_result: The Hospital HMI / lane UI accepts both a tote-add operation and a tote-remove operation without the reported hospital induction restriction.
steps.healthy_condition: The hospital station visibly permits tote additions and removals, matching the restored state reported in the incident.
steps.failure_condition: The Hospital HMI / lane UI still permits removal but does not permit addition, or either tote operation remains unavailable.

actions.label: Test tote operations
actions.exact_action: Verify on the Hospital HMI / lane UI that the hospital station can add and remove totes again.

stop_or_escalate_if: Totes cannot be added after the recovery actions.
Totes cannot be removed or the Hospital HMI / lane UI remains unavailable.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The site reported that it could add and remove totes again.
The hospital area could remove totes but could not add them.

steps.title: Confirm robots and system are running
steps.purpose: Verify that the hospital recovery restored robot availability and overall system operation.
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI / lane UI and the live Apidog / WCS API state, confirm that the affected robots have been re-added and are operating. Confirm that the system is running after recovery.
steps.expected_result: The affected robots are shown as re-added and operating, and the live system state is running.
steps.healthy_condition: The Hospital HMI / lane UI supports ongoing tote flow, the affected robots are back up and running, and the system is reported as running.
steps.failure_condition: A robot cannot be re-added or remains unavailable, tote flow is not restored, or the system is not running.

actions.label: Verify robot and system state
actions.exact_action: Confirm that the robots are re-added and back up and running, and confirm that the system is running.

stop_or_escalate_if: Robots cannot be re-added or are not back up and running.
The system is not running after the supported recovery actions.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The site reported that all robots were re-added and back up and running.
The issue was reported resolved by 9:00 PM ET and the system was running.

success_criteria: The Hospital HMI / lane UI accepts tote additions and removals.
The affected robots are re-added and shown as back up and running.
The live system is running after recovery.
No undocumented Apidog / WCS API or AGV state change was performed.
healthy_conditions: The Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU remains paused during recovery when operators are not present at the tippers.
The Apidog / WCS API state no longer shows the targeted inducted or disconnected tote as blocking hospital flow.
Affected AGVs are present in the expected live system state and are available for operation.
The Hospital HMI / lane UI supports both tote add and tote remove operations.
failure_conditions: The Hospital HMI / lane UI still cannot add totes.
The targeted inducted or disconnected tote cannot be removed through the identifiable supported Apidog / WCS API action.
An affected AGV remains disconnected, obstructed, incorrectly located, or cannot be re-added.
The required API or AGV recovery action is not identifiable on the live surface.
The system is not running after recovery.
escalation_guidance: Escalate to L2/L3 review if the tote cannot be removed through the supported Apidog / WCS API action, the AGV association remains disconnected, or the Hospital HMI / lane UI still cannot add or remove totes.
Stop before any API or AGV state change that is not explicitly identifiable from the live Apidog / WCS API state.
Escalate the unresolved condition rather than assigning a definitive root cause; the incident recorded multiple possible contributing conditions.
Coordinate with the site operator if the Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU pause state cannot be established.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Summary documents removal of an inducted tote with API dog, removal of tote 51 when it could not be removed from hospital, removal of several AGVs, and pausing the station at the tippers during recovery.
AVEVA was described as using the same endpoints as API dog; the incident discussion also described removing an AGV from a zone and adding a tote to a station.
The original issue was resolved and the site was able to add and remove totes again.
The site reported that all robots were re-added and back up and running.

content.text: Use this path when a hospital station cannot add or induct totes, a robot appears shut down, or the site cannot start or sustain sort. Confirm the observable impact, check for AGV location or tote-association anomalies, consider the source-supported service and lane recovery path, and validate tote flow and site operation.

structured_payload.title: Hospital tote-induct or site-flow disruption with AGV state anomalies
structured_payload.user_facing_summary: Use this path when a hospital station cannot add or induct totes, a robot appears shut down, or the site cannot start or sustain sort. Confirm the observable impact, check for AGV location or tote-association anomalies, consider the source-supported service and lane recovery path, and validate tote flow and site operation.
structured_payload.playbook_goal: Restore safe hospital tote flow and broader site operation by distinguishing a localized hospital workflow problem from an AGV/tote-state or service-related disruption, applying only authorized high-level recovery actions, and validating stable operation.

nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to confirm with the site whether totes can be added and removed at the affected hospital station, whether the reported robot or station is shut down, whether sort can start or remain running, and what the Hospital HMI or related HMI view visibly reports.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: Site operator or support user confirms the affected workflow through a site interview and, when available, the Hospital HMI or related HMI view. Healthy signal: totes can be added and removed and sort is operating normally. nodes.primary_action: Ask the site/operator to confirm—using the currently visible Hospital HMI or their live workflow observation—whether totes can be added/inducted and removed at the affected hospital station, and whether sort is able to start and remain operating (and whether the reported robot/AGV is in a shut down condition).
evidence_to_collect: Whether the hospital station accepts tote add/induct (confirmation from the operator or read-only HMI indication).
Whether the hospital station allows tote removal (confirmation from the operator or read-only HMI indication).
Whether sort can start and remain operating (site confirmation and any visible HMI status indicator).
Whether the reported robot/AGV is shown as shut down (site confirmation and/or visible station/robot status indicator).
If HMI evidence is unreadable, capture the limitation (which labels/status meanings are not readable and why).
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Site confirms totes can be added/inducted and removed normally at the hospital station, and sort starts and remains operating normally (and the station/robot is not reported as shut down).
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Hospital tote addition/induction is unavailable (totes can be removed but not added/inducted), or the station/robot is reported as shut down, or sort cannot start or does not sustain operation; hospital backlog continues to increase.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: The site/operator cannot identify the affected workflow or the available HMI/status image is unreadable/ambiguous, or the report appears historical rather than current.

optional_corroboration.note: If the site reports shut down and sort disruption, corroborate with a hospital HMI operations/induct-extract status screen to reduce ambiguity from unreadable screenshots before branching into deeper AGV/tote or service diagnostics.

nodes.generated_guidance: Use this node only to confirm whether the incident symptoms still match the entry pattern for this playbook path (hospital tote-induct blocked and/or sort not starting/sustaining, with possible robot/AGV shut down). Do not assume root cause. If the site confirms recovery already restored tote add/remove and stable sort, exit this playbook path rather than continuing diagnostics.

ontology_evidence.text: Model CellCodeDatabaseModel (robotics): Stores all cell codes in the map. When a new AGV is added to the system while in a running state, the system first checks if the AGV's current cell code is in a missing zone under the sorter; if not, it uses this table to look up which hospital the cell code is connected to and sends an Initialize command to Geek.. nodes.purpose: Determine whether the current report is an active hospital tote-induct problem, a broader sort disruption, or a localized condition that does not match this response path.

evidence_collection_procedures.title: WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) AGV state inspection
evidence_collection_procedures.purpose: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) live read-only database surface to inspect robotics-related AGV state records when the RMS / fleet status UI reports AGVs out of sync or the robotic system is stopped. Compare the populated SSMS State results with the live RMS / fleet status UI; the listed state values do not independently establish a fault.

nodes.question: Determine whether the current report is an active hospital tote-induct problem, a broader sort disruption, or a localized condition that does not match this response path.

node_interpretation_mapping.success: Hospital tote add/induct and remove are both available; sort can start and remains operating normally.
node_interpretation_mapping.failure: Hospital tote addition/induction is blocked (even if removal works), and/or robot/AGV shown shut down, and/or sort cannot start or does not sustain.
node_interpretation_mapping.inconclusive: Site cannot confirm active workflow behavior or HMI evidence is unreadable/ambiguous or historical only.

nodes.title: Check for AGV location, roster, and tote-association anomalies
nodes.intent: Determine whether the reported hospital-flow problem coincides with an AGV in an unexpected location, duplicate occupancy, disconnected tote, or residual tote association.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the reported hospital-flow problem coincides with an AGV in an unexpected location, duplicate occupancy, disconnected tote, or residual tote association.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to compare the affected AGV or robot location and rack occupancy with the expected fleet or station state using the source-referenced HMI/layout view, the source-supported operational view or fleet status view, and API/Aveva state view when available; the procedure should also identify residual or disconnected tote associations without prescribing data mutations.
nodes.source_supported_description: Teams messages and annotated HMI-style images describe an AGV in an unexpected location, two AGVs under a rack, and possible disconnected or residual tote associations.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to compare the affected AGV or robot location and rack occupancy with the expected fleet or station state using the source-referenced HMI/layout view, the source-supported operational view or fleet status view, and API/Aveva state view when available; the procedure should also identify residual or disconnected tote associations without prescribing data mutations.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: Site operator or support user observes the physical or displayed AGV state using the available HMI/layout view, the source-supported operational view or fleet view when available, and the source-referenced API/Aveva state-management interface. Healthy signal: AGVs occupy expected locations and no disconnected or residual tote association is reported. Unhealthy signal: an AGV is reported in an unexpected location, multiple AGVs appear under one rack or in one location, an AGV is absent from an expected rack, or a disconnected/associated tote remains in the system. Inconclusive: identifiers, locations, or tote associations cannot be confirmed from the available view.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Chat states that Aveva was used to remove an AGV from a zone and add a tote to a station, and that Aveva hits the same endpoints as API dog.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The packet includes a possible zone/location mismatch, but not a confirmed pairing failure.

backend_mappings.note: No SQL model documents a dedicated pairing/pair-fail state as such; this cross-links zone_pairing_state to the same robot-location/roster backend evidence used by device_roster_state, since an 'unable to get a pair' symptom is operationally a roster/location mismatch (an AGV missing/duplicated at the expected zone location). Do not treat this as a source-confirmed pairing-specific SQL model.

backend_observability.note: No SQL model documents a dedicated pairing/pair-fail state as such; this cross-links zone_pairing_state to the same robot-location/roster backend evidence used by device_roster_state, since an 'unable to get a pair' symptom is operationally a roster/location mismatch (an AGV missing/duplicated at the expected zone location). Do not treat this as a source-confirmed pairing-specific SQL model.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology does not provide a specific backend mapping for the source-described disconnected tote and rack-occupancy evidence.
healthy_indicators: AGVs are shown or confirmed in expected locations.
Expected racks or stations have the expected AGV occupancy.
No disconnected or residual tote association is reported.
The hospital station's displayed tote state is consistent with physical operation.
unhealthy_indicators: AGV is reported not to belong in the displayed location.
Two AGVs appear under the same rack or in the same zone.
A rack or expected location is missing an AGV.
An AGV is associated with a disconnected or residual tote.
Hospital tote state cannot be reconciled with the displayed AGV state.
inconclusive_indicators: AGV identifiers or rack labels are unreadable.
The display is only an annotated image without a reliable legend.
Physical and displayed locations cannot be compared.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: This AGV doesn't belong here; two AGVs were under the rack in the same zone.
AGV with disconnected tote was in the system; other AGVs were under the rack.
Aveva was used to remove an AGV from a zone and add a tote to a station.

nodes.primary_action: Correlate the reported hospital-flow disruption with AGV roster/location and tote-association state by checking the displayed HMI/layout (as available) and confirming the AGV(s) and tote association state with a fleet view and backend read-only evidence; identify whether anomalies exist such as unexpected locations, duplicate occupancy, missing expected AGVs, or residual/disconnected tote associations.
nodes.primary_surface: rms_ui + aveva_hmi (and corroborate with wcs_sql read-only backend evidence as required)
evidence_to_collect: AGV/robot state and location for the reported affected AGV(s)/zone(s) from the displayed fleet/map/HMI view.
Any indication of duplicate occupancy (e.g., two AGVs under one rack/zone).
Any indication of missing expected AGV from an expected rack/location.
Tote association indicators: whether a tote appears disconnected/residual or inconsistent between displayed station/rack context and the system.
Freshness: confirm evidence is current (not only historical) using the view timestamps/time references when available.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: AGVs occupy expected locations/occupancy and the system does not show disconnected/residual tote associations; hospital tote state is consistent with displayed operation.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: An AGV is in an unexpected location, duplicate occupancy is observed (two AGVs under one rack/zone), an expected AGV is absent from a rack/location, and/or a disconnected/residual tote association persists; hospital tote state cannot be reconciled with displayed AGV state.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: AGV identifiers, rack labels, or locations cannot be confirmed due to unreadable labels, or physical vs displayed locations cannot be reconciled from available evidence.

optional_corroboration.note: If you suspect disconnected tote associations, corroborate using a read-only fleet view before any state-correcting recovery is attempted, and ensure any later recovery uses an approved API/Aveva or physical procedure.

nodes.generated_guidance: This node decides whether to proceed to authorized high-level recovery (node_4) based on evidence of AGV/location and/or tote-association anomalies. Do not mutate data here; only identify and document the anomalies and whether they are currently active.

ontology_evidence.title: WCS model — RobotDatabaseModel

source_refs.note: PascalCase model inventory; live query screenshot on p.77 supplied the full column list and example values

ontology_evidence.text: Model RobotDatabaseModel (robotics): Robot/AGV live state: contains the data for every robot in the system including its state, tote name, assigned sorter side, current/destination location, and state.. Fields: Name: Robot code / AGV identifier (e.g. 1555058).; State: Robot state enum (Tipper/Hospital/Charger/Sorter/GLD/ShutDown family). Observed live values include SWaitingInzone, Removed, SWaitingForExchange, GoCharge, MovingToChargerEntranceQueue, MovingToTipperQueue.; ToteId: Tote currently

source_refs.note: PascalCase model inventory; live query screenshot on p.72 resolved SorterId/StagingId/QueueId/Sequence/SorterSideDatabaseModelId column names
candidate_training_video_d2_sorter_zone_exit_queue_sequence_mapping_lookup (quarantined Day2 candidate; procedure-level detail, not a schema dump)

ontology_evidence.text: Model SortLocationsDatabaseModel (robotics): Contains all the sorter locations and their respective queue locations. The queue location is the location behind the sorter location where the AGV with an empty tote will move to fill when an exchange happens. Also a zone/shutdown-queue-sequence -> station/location mapping lookup used to translate a shutdown queue sequence number tied to a zone into the target sorter station/location.. Fields: SorterId: The sorter (sort) location id — FK into RobotLo

nodes.title: Determine whether the hospital-station service condition is contributing
nodes.intent: Determine whether the reported AGV hospital-station server or OptiSweep service condition is present and sufficiently correlated with the hospital or site-flow symptoms.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the reported AGV hospital-station server or OptiSweep service condition is present and sufficiently correlated with the hospital or site-flow symptoms.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to review the incident's AGV hospital-station and OptiSweep service evidence, inspect Windows Event Viewer and Windows Services for current service health when access is authorized, and correlate that state with Hospital Lane or HMI responsiveness without assuming that the historical reset note proves a current fault.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source documents AGV hospital-station server issues, a need to reset services, and a closure statement that OptiSweep services were reset before Hospital Lane was restarted.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to review the incident's AGV hospital-station and OptiSweep service evidence, inspect Windows Event Viewer and Windows Services for current service health when access is authorized, and correlate that state with Hospital Lane or HMI responsiveness without assuming that the historical reset note proves a current fault.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1 or L2 support inspects the source-named service evidence in the available work-order or service notes and, where authorized, Windows Event Viewer or Windows Services for the affected host; the site or support user may also confirm Hospital Lane or HMI responsiveness. Healthy signal: the relevant service and hospital interface are responsive and no current abnormal service condition is evident. Unhealthy signal: current evidence shows an AGV hospital-station server or OptiSweep service abnormality, the hospital interface is unresponsive, or service-reset context coincides with the reported disruption. Inconclusive: the source only contains a historical note saying services need reset, without current status or named service details.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The packet identifies a Windows-services-related artifact and repeatedly documents AGV hospital-station server issues and a need to reset services, although the visible artifact is a notes pane rather than a live Event Viewer screen.
The source explicitly states that AGV hospital-station services need to be reset and that OptiSweep services were reset in the closure summary.
The packet includes hospital/rack HMI-style screenshots and references Hospital Lane operation.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology does not identify the exact OptiSweep service names or map the historical service-note artifact to current service-state fields.
healthy_indicators: Authorized support confirms the relevant service is running and responsive.
Hospital Lane or the related HMI responds normally.
No current service abnormality is found.
unhealthy_indicators: Current evidence shows a stopped, repeatedly failing, or otherwise abnormal relevant service.
Hospital Lane or its related HMI remains unresponsive while service health is abnormal.
A current service condition correlates with the inability to induct or start sort.
inconclusive_indicators: Only a historical note says services need reset.
The exact service names or host are not identified.
The available artifact is a notes pane rather than a live service-status view.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: AGV hospital station is having server issues; services need to be reset.

nodes.primary_action: Verify whether the current AGV hospital-station server and/or OptiSweep service condition is present and correlated with Hospital Lane/HMI responsiveness. Inspect the named service evidence where available and, when authorized, check Windows Event Viewer and Windows Services for current OptiSweep/WCSWebApplication failures or restart activity; corroborate with whether Hospital Lane/HMI responsiveness matches the suspected time window.
nodes.primary_surface: event_viewer (Windows Event Viewer/Services) with hospital_hmi responsiveness corroboration
evidence_to_collect: Current Windows Event Viewer and Services evidence related to OptiSweep/WCSWebApplication (e.g., crash/restart or stopped services).
Whether the hospital interface (Hospital Lane/HMI) responds normally vs unresponsive.
Service restart/correlation: whether the observed service issues align temporally with the tote-induct block and/or inability to start sort.
Service details: exact service names and host if present in evidence; if not available, document the gap.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Relevant service is running and responsive; Hospital Lane/HMI responds normally; no current abnormal service condition is evident.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Current evidence shows relevant service abnormality (stopped/crashing/restarting); Hospital Lane/HMI is unresponsive and/or correlates with the disruption window.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Evidence is only historical (e.g., 'services need reset') without current service-state details; exact services/host not identified or artifact is not a live status screen.

optional_corroboration.note: If the hospital interface appears down while services evidence is inconclusive, corroborate with any available OptiSweep/WCS API or Ignition Gateway responsiveness evidence only when those surfaces are accessible and supported for the chosen node scope.

nodes.generated_guidance: Do not treat historical 'reset needed' notes as proof of a current fault. This node is about current condition and correlation to the hospital/sort symptom set. If services look healthy (or evidence is inconclusive), shift back to AGV/tote anomaly investigation (node_2). If services look abnormal and an authorized recovery procedure is available, proceed to node_4.

ontology_evidence.title: Capability — Hospital diversion / lane routing
ontology_evidence.text: Capability hospital_diversion: Confirm hospital diversion path: lanes, stacklight, hospital tags/locations, AGV routing to hospital.. When: Hospital diversion active or suspected; stacklight/lane alarms; robots diverting unexpectedly. Not for: Generic tipper fault without hospital context.. Surfaces: rms_ui, hospital_hmi, wcs_sql, site_interview, building_acb_hmi. nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed for the authorized recovery path selected from the diagnosis: reset or recover the named OptiSweep or AGV hospital-station services and restart Hospital Lane when approved; alternatively use the approved API dog or Aveva procedure for supported tote or AGV state correction; include site safety controls, role limits, and conditions for any physical AGV removal. nodes.source_supported_description: Historical evidence describes service reset and Hospital Lane restart, API dog removal of tote state, Aveva-based AGV/tote state correction, and removal of several AGVs during recovery. These actions are preserved as high-level source evidence, not procedural instructions.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed for the authorized recovery path selected from the diagnosis: reset or recover the named OptiSweep or AGV hospital-station services and restart Hospital Lane when approved; alternatively use the approved API dog or Aveva procedure for supported tote or AGV state correction; include site safety controls, role limits, and conditions for any physical AGV removal. Exact commands, click paths, and mutation steps belong in the linked runbook.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: Authorized support or site personnel complete the applicable approved recovery and record whether it completed. Recovery signal: the source-supported service or lane recovery is completed, or the affected AGV/tote state is corrected through the approved API/Aveva or physical procedure. Unsuccessful signal: the action cannot be completed, the state remains abnormal, or the action introduces additional tote or AGV discrepancies. Inconclusive: the source does not identify the exact service, authorization, or safe physical conditions required.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Source notes state that services needed to be reset, and the closure summary states OptiSweep services were reset.

ontology_gaps: The source does not identify the exact OptiSweep services, API operation names, physical isolation requirements, or authorization boundaries for the historical recovery actions.
healthy_indicators: Authorized recovery completed; affected hospital tote flow or AGV/tote state is corrected.
unhealthy_indicators: Recovery cannot be completed safely or completed but state remains abnormal.
inconclusive_indicators: The recovery action or authorization is not supported by a named procedure.

nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Do not perform a service reset, API/Aveva state mutation, or physical AGV handling unless the responsible role has an approved procedure and the required safety and authorization conditions are met.

nodes.primary_action: Perform only authorized recovery corresponding to the confirmed condition: reset/recover the identified OptiSweep or AGV hospital-station services and restart Hospital Lane (when approved); or correct supported AGV/tote state through the approved API/Aveva pathway; or complete an approved physical AGV handling/removal only under site safety/authorization conditions. Then record completion status and whether the abnormal state is cleared.
nodes.primary_surface: wcs_api (Apidog) + aveva_hmi + event_viewer-validated service context; physical_floor only if approved for removal
evidence_to_collect: Completion confirmation that the authorized recovery action was successfully completed (service reset and Hospital Lane restart OR API/Aveva state correction OR approved physical AGV handling/removal).
Post-action observable result: hospital tote add/induct availability, and whether abnormal AGV/tote state is corrected (as defined by subsequent node validation).
If recovery fails: document which part could not be completed and what new discrepancies appeared.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: The authorized recovery is completed and the affected service/lane or AGV/tote state is corrected without introducing additional tote/AGV discrepancies.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: The action cannot be completed, the state remains abnormal, or the action introduces additional tote/AGV discrepancies.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Authorization/safe physical conditions cannot be confirmed, or the packet does not identify the exact service/AGV/tote/physical location in a way that a safe authorized procedure can be selected.

optional_corroboration.note: If the selected recovery path is API/Aveva based, corroborate via the read-only evidence surfaces in the next validation node rather than assuming success from UI responsiveness alone.

nodes.expected_or_observed_result: Site operator observes tote handling and sort operation, while authorized support checks the relevant service or API/Aveva status used during recovery. Healthy signal: totes can be added and removed, Hospital Lane accepts normal flow, AGVs are re-added or operating in expected locations, movement resumes, and sort starts and remains stable. Unhealthy signal: tote addition remains blocked, AGVs remain stopped or misplaced, disconnected tote state persists, or sort fails again. Inconclusive: only a general statement that the system is running is available without confirmation of hospital tote flow and residual AGV/tote state.

evidence_to_collect: Hospital HMI/site evidence that tote add/induct and tote remove both work at the hospital station.
Evidence that Hospital Lane accepts normal flow and sort starts and remains stable.
WCS/SSMS read-only AGV state and location consistency after recovery (no duplicate occupancy/misplaced robots; expected roster presence).
Evidence that there is no disconnected/residual tote association persisting after recovery.

nodes.healthy_interpretation: Totes can be added and removed; Hospital Lane accepts normal flow; AGVs are operating in expected locations/roster is consistent; movement resumes and sort remains stable; no disconnected/residual tote association is reported.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Hospital tote addition remains blocked; AGVs remain stopped/misplaced/duplicated/absent; disconnected tote state persists; sort fails again during monitoring.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Only a general statement that the system is running exists without confirmation of hospital tote-add behavior and residual AGV/tote state; HMI/API/Aveva view unreadable; insufficient monitoring interval.

optional_corroboration.note: If residual state is suspected, repeat only the minimal read-only evidence checks needed to confirm whether the residual tote/AGV inconsistency persists before initiating any additional recovery steps.

nodes.generated_guidance: Do not declare victory based on 'system running' alone. Validation must explicitly cover hospital tote add/induct behavior and confirm AGV/tote consistency via read-only backend evidence.

source_refs.note: PascalCase model inventory

ontology_evidence.text: Model CellCodeDatabaseModel (robotics): Stores all cell codes in the map. When a new AGV is added to the system while in a running state, the system first checks if the AGV's current cell code is in a missing zone under the sorter; if not, it uses this table to look up which hospital the cell code is connected to and sends an Initialize command to Geek.. ontology_evidence.text: Model SortLocationsDatabaseModel (robotics): Contains all the sorter locations and their respective queue locations. The queue location is the location behind the sorter location where the AGV with an empty tote will move to fill when an exchange happens. Also a zone/shutdown-queue-sequence -> station/location mapping lookup used to translate a shutdown queue sequence number tied to a zone into the target sorter station/location.. nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to interview the site about whether the affected hospital station can add and remove totes, inspect the Hospital HMI or other source-evidenced hospital layout view for the affected station, and compare the displayed AGV placement and tote association with the operator's physical observation.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator observes the hospital station and reports whether tote removal works while tote addition fails; the operator or L1 support checks the hospital HMI or readable layout view for the affected station and reports whether an AGV is shown in an unexpected location or whether multiple AGVs appear associated with one rack or zone. Healthy signal: tote add and remove both work and no abnormal AGV or tote association is reported. Unhealthy signal: tote add or induction fails, especially with an unexpected AGV or associated tote. Inconclusive: the site cannot reproduce the symptom or the displayed location/association is unreadable.

nodes.primary_action: Confirm, with the site operator, that the problem is specifically hospital tote addition/induction (not a general outage), and capture whether tote removal works while induction fails; then verify on the hospital layout/HMI whether an AGV/rack/zone appears in an unexpected location or multiple AGVs share the same rack/zone.

evidence_to_collect: Site confirmation: hospital tote add/induct works or fails; tote removal works or fails

nodes.healthy_interpretation: Both tote add/induct and tote removal work at the hospital station, and no abnormal AGV placement or duplicate occupancy pattern is visible/confirmed.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Hospital tote add/induct fails (especially while removal works), and the hospital view indicates an unexpected AGV placement and/or duplicate occupancy, supporting an AGV/tote state inconsistency context.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: The symptom cannot be reproduced/confirmed by the site operator, or the hospital view/labels are unreadable or the evidence conflicts (operator vs displayed state).

optional_corroboration.note: If hospital induction failure appears tied to AGV location/state mismatch, corroborate the affected AGV roster/location state using RMS/HMI and backend read-only evidence before proceeding to any state-changing correction.

nodes.generated_guidance: Use the site interview to establish add vs remove asymmetry, then use the hospital station read-only screens to confirm whether the displayed AGV/rack/zone context matches the anomaly described in the incident notes. If the evidence cannot be read or the symptom is not reproducible, do not assume a mismatch; go to escalation after confirming ambiguity.

node_interpretation_mapping.success: Hospital tote add/induct works and tote removal works; no relevant unexpected AGV placement/duplicate occupancy is shown.

nodes.title: Determine whether AGV and tote state is inconsistent
nodes.intent: Determine whether an AGV removal, unexpected location, duplicate rack occupancy, or disconnected tote association is present and plausibly connected to the hospital induction symptom.
nodes.goal: Determine whether an AGV removal, unexpected location, duplicate rack occupancy, or disconnected tote association is present and plausibly connected to the hospital induction symptom.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect the hospital rack or AGV layout view and, where authorized, the API dog or Aveva-fed AGV and tote state for unexpected AGV placement, duplicate location occupancy, removed-AGV residue, or disconnected tote association; the procedure should define how to record evidence without changing state.
nodes.source_supported_description: The packet repeatedly discusses an AGV in the wrong location, multiple AGVs under a rack, a disconnected tote, and use of API dog or Aveva to correct AGV and tote state.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect the hospital rack or AGV layout view and, where authorized, the API dog or Aveva-fed AGV and tote state for unexpected AGV placement, duplicate location occupancy, removed-AGV residue, or disconnected tote association; the procedure should define how to record evidence without changing state.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The operator observes the physical or displayed AGV position, while L1/L2 support reviews the source-evidenced AGV/layout or API client context when available. Healthy signal: the expected AGV is associated with the expected station or rack and no disconnected tote is present. Unhealthy signal: an AGV is in an unexpected location, two AGVs are shown under one rack or in one zone, or a tote remains associated with an unavailable or removed AGV. Inconclusive: the source view lacks readable identifiers or the association cannot be confirmed.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Annotated HMI-style rack/layout screenshot was shared alongside the statement that an AGV did not belong in the location.
The packet states that Aveva was used to remove an AGV from a zone and add a tote to a station.

ontology_gaps: No supplied ontology card establishes the backend model or fields for AGV-to-tote association or hospital-station tote ownership.
healthy_indicators: AGV location and station association agree with the expected layout.
No disconnected or orphaned tote association is observed.
unhealthy_indicators: AGV is displayed in an unexpected location.
Two AGVs appear under one rack or in one zone.
A tote remains associated with a removed or disconnected AGV.
inconclusive_indicators: Only a low-resolution annotated layout is available.
The interface does not expose a readable roster, location, or tote association.
The reported anomaly is based only on second-hand discussion.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Summary describes an AGV with a disconnected tote, removal of an inducted tote through API dog, and removal of additional AGVs to restore flow.
Chat says Aveva hits the same endpoints as API dog and was used to remove an AGV from a zone and add a tote to a station.

nodes.primary_action: Determine whether there is a credible AGV/tote inconsistency connected to the hospital induction failure by checking the hospital-view context and then confirming backend-consistent roster/location indications (especially unexpected placement and duplicate occupancy), without changing state.
nodes.performed_by: L1_support / L2_support (remote evidence review) with operator assistance for any needed station observation
nodes.primary_surface: rms_ui with corroboration via wcs_sql (read-only) when feasible
evidence_to_collect: Hospital-view evidence (unexpected AGV placement and/or duplicate occupancy under a rack/zone) for the station involved

Backend-correlated AGV roster/location state for the anomaly: confirm whether an AGV is in an unexpected location, duplicate occupancy exists, and whether any tote appears disconnected/orphaned (as evidenced by tote association differences)
Whether the anomaly is uniquely identifiable (robot/AGV identity, rack/zone mapping) or not
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Hospital-view anomaly is not present/confirmable and backend roster/location state does not indicate unexpected placement or duplicate occupancy; no disconnected/orphan tote evidence is present.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Backend-correlated evidence supports an inconsistency: an AGV is in an unexpected location, duplicate occupancy exists, and/or a tote remains associated with a removed/disconnected AGV.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: The station/rack/AGV/tote identifiers in the evidence are unreadable, or the reported anomaly cannot be confirmed from available interfaces without guesswork.

optional_corroboration.note: If the symptom pattern is consistent with a roster/location mismatch (zone pairing / expected occupancy), corroborate via one backend read-only robotics model (robot location/roster) even if the RMS/hospital view seems to show the issue.

nodes.generated_guidance: Treat the operator/hospital-view observation as historical evidence; confirm the current AGV roster/location context for the discussed rack/zone before performing any authorized recovery. If the evidence cannot uniquely identify the affected AGV/tote mapping, stop and escalate rather than performing state-changing corrections.

ontology_evidence.title: WCS model — CellCodeDatabaseModel

source_refs.note: PascalCase model inventory

ontology_evidence.text: Model CellCodeDatabaseModel (robotics): Stores all cell codes in the map. When a new AGV is added to the system while in a running state, the system first checks if the AGV's current cell code is in a missing zone under the sorter; if not, it uses this table to look up which hospital the cell code is connected to and sends an Initialize command to Geek.. Fields: CellCode: Cell/node code analogous to an RMS node code (vendor-agnostic).; X: X coordinate for the cell code.; Y: Y coordinate for the

source_refs.note: PascalCase model inventory; live query screenshot on p.72 resolved SorterId/StagingId/QueueId/Sequence/SorterSideDatabaseModelId column names
candidate_training_video_d2_sorter_zone_exit_queue_sequence_mapping_lookup (quarantined Day2 candidate; procedure-level detail, not a schema dump)

ontology_evidence.text: Model SortLocationsDatabaseModel (robotics): Contains all the sorter locations and their respective queue locations. The queue location is the location behind the sorter location where the AGV with an empty tote will move to fill when an exchange happens. Also a zone/shutdown-queue-sequence -> station/location mapping lookup used to translate a shutdown queue sequence number tied to a zone into the target sorter station/location.. Fields: SorterId: The sorter (sort) location id — FK into RobotLo

nodes.intent: Use an authorized, source-supported recovery procedure to correct the affected AGV or tote state when the diagnostic evidence identifies a supported mismatch.
nodes.goal: Use an authorized, source-supported recovery procedure to correct the affected AGV or tote state when the diagnostic evidence identifies a supported mismatch.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed for authorized AGV and tote-state correction using the source-evidenced Aveva or API dog interface, including safety prerequisites, role limits, handling of an inducted or disconnected tote, and evidence capture; exact API actions and screen steps belong in the procedure.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source reports high-level use of API dog and Aveva to remove totes, remove an AGV from a zone, and add a tote to a station; it does not provide the exact procedure.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed for authorized AGV and tote-state correction using the source-evidenced Aveva or API dog interface, including safety prerequisites, role limits, handling of an inducted or disconnected tote, and evidence capture; exact API actions and screen steps belong in the procedure.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The authorized operator or support role observes that the targeted AGV or tote state has been corrected in the approved interface. Progress signal: the stale or disconnected association is removed or the expected station association is restored. Unhealthy signal: the interface rejects the correction, the state remains inconsistent, or the action would require an unapproved physical or database change. Inconclusive: the source interface does not show a reliable post-action state.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The packet states that the site used Aveva to remove an AGV from a zone and add a tote to a station.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not provide a validated capability card for the specific mutating AGV or tote correction operation.
healthy_indicators: Approved interface reflects the intended AGV or tote association.
The affected hospital station can proceed to validation.
unhealthy_indicators: Correction is rejected or produces a new inconsistent association.
A tote remains stuck or disconnected after the authorized action.
inconclusive_indicators: The interface does not provide a reliable state confirmation.

nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Do not continue with state-changing actions if the authorized interface, target association, or safety preconditions cannot be confirmed.

nodes.primary_action: Apply an authorized correction to restore the AGV/tote state mismatch using the approved source-evidenced interface (Aveva or API dog). Only proceed after identifying the specific affected AGV/tote association mismatch; otherwise stop and escalate.
nodes.performed_by: operator (with L1_support/L2_support oversight as needed for authorization and safety)
evidence_to_collect: Pre-action: confirm the exact target mismatch (which AGV/zone/rack/tote association is stale) is identifiable
Action acceptance: whether the approved interface accepts the correction and does not reject it
Post-action evidence: updated association/placement consistent with the intended correction (evidence must be visible/confirmable in the same approved interface)
nodes.healthy_interpretation: The approved interface reflects the intended AGV/tote association correction, and hospital validation can proceed.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: The correction is rejected, produces a new inconsistent association, or leaves tote/AGV association ambiguous.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: The interface cannot provide a reliable post-action state confirmation, or safety/role preconditions for the correction cannot be met.

optional_corroboration.note: After completing the authorized correction, corroborate the updated roster/location state using backend read-only evidence before declaring recovery.

nodes.generated_guidance: This node performs only recovery steps after diagnostic confirmation. Do not improvise or perform unapproved physical/database changes. Capture before/after evidence from the authorized interface so the validation gate can determine success.

selected_procedure.purpose: Use the System HMI API screen’s AGVs section to remove a problematic AGV by ID, recover (add back) the AGV by ID after physical recovery, and pause/resume all AGV movement fleet-wide.

nodes.selection_rationale: Retrieval realigned to fleet/status-check runbook; prior link penalized for intent mismatch.
prerequisites: You have the target AGV ID to enter into the Remove AGV and Recover AGV fields.
Access to the System HMI API screen with the AGVs section (AGV API Controls)
safety_checks: If the AGV has a tote, take the tote to the hospital where the tote is removed; the tote is recovered when it is put back in the system.
nodes.success_confirmation: Remove AGV is followed by physical removal of the AGV from the system; if a tote is present, the tote is taken to the hospital where the tote is removed.
nodes.failure_boundary: Cannot physically remove/recover the AGV/tote as required after using Remove AGV.

runbook_execution_result.success: Remove AGV is followed by physical removal of the AGV from the system; if a tote is present, the tote is taken to the hospital where the tote is removed.
runbook_execution_result.failure: Cannot physically remove/recover the AGV/tote as required after using Remove AGV.

nodes.title: Validate hospital tote flow and AGV recovery
nodes.intent: Confirm that the hospital station accepts totes again and that the affected AGV and tote state no longer prevents normal flow.
nodes.goal: Confirm that the hospital station accepts totes again and that the affected AGV and tote state no longer prevents normal flow.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to validate hospital-station tote add and remove behavior, confirm the affected AGV roster or location state through the source-evidenced hospital or AGV view, and monitor for continued backlog or recurrence before declaring the hospital flow recovered.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source reports restoration of adding and removing totes and that all robots were re-added and running.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to validate hospital-station tote add and remove behavior, confirm the affected AGV roster or location state through the source-evidenced hospital or AGV view, and monitor for continued backlog or recurrence before declaring the hospital flow recovered.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator observes the hospital station and performs the approved validation activity. Healthy signal: totes can be added and removed at the hospital, AGVs are re-added or operating as expected, and movement resumes. Unhealthy signal: tote addition remains unavailable, an AGV remains shut down or misplaced, or backlog continues to grow. Inconclusive: only a general statement that the system is running is available without a hospital-specific tote-flow check.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Case comments state that the site was able to add and remove totes again and that all robots were re-added and running.
The packet includes an HMI-style hospital-area layout screenshot used during the tote and AGV investigation.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology does not provide a detailed validation mapping for hospital tote-flow recovery.
healthy_indicators: Site confirms totes can be added and removed.
Robots are re-added and back up and running.
Movement resumes without immediate recurrence.
unhealthy_indicators: Hospital still cannot accept or induct totes.
AGVs remain shut down, misplaced, or associated with disconnected totes.
Hospital backlog or tote-flow disruption continues.
inconclusive_indicators: Only a general 'system running' message is available.
Validation is not performed at the hospital station.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: If hospital tote flow fails after the supported correction or the AGV/tote state remains ambiguous, stop this path and use the escalation gate.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Site was able to add and remove totes and all robots were re-added and back up and running.

nodes.primary_action: Validate hospital tote flow recovery by confirming the hospital station can add/induct and remove totes again, and ensure any previously affected AGV(s) are re-added/operating normally (no immediate recurrence).
nodes.primary_surface: hospital_hmi (plus site_interview for on-floor behavior confirmation)
evidence_to_collect: Site observation: tote add/induct works at the hospital station
Site observation: tote removal continues to work
Confirmation that AGVs/robots are re-added and not remaining shut down/misplaced for the affected context
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Totes can be added and removed at the hospital, and movement resumes; affected robots are re-added or operating normally without immediate backlog/recurrence.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Tote addition/induction remains unavailable, and/or AGVs remain shut down/misplaced/associated with disconnected totes; backlog continues.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Only general 'system running' statements are available; a hospital-specific tote-flow check was not performed or cannot be confirmed.

optional_corroboration.note: If hospital HMI indicates the station still cannot induct, corroborate with RMS read-only fleet/roster state to ensure the update is not stale before escalating.

nodes.generated_guidance: Do not rely solely on the system-wide 'running' status. Validation must be specific to the hospital station’s add/induct and remove behavior, and should confirm there is no persistent AGV/tote inconsistency preventing flow.

source_refs.note: PascalCase model inventory

ontology_evidence.text: Model CellCodeDatabaseModel (robotics): Stores all cell codes in the map. When a new AGV is added to the system while in a running state, the system first checks if the AGV's current cell code is in a missing zone under the sorter; if not, it uses this table to look up which hospital the cell code is connected to and sends an Initialize command to Geek.. Fields: CellCode: Cell/node code analogous to an RMS node code (vendor-agnostic).; X: X coordinate for the cell code.; Y: Y coordinate for the

ontology_evidence.text: Model RobotDatabaseModel (robotics): Robot/AGV live state: contains the data for every robot in the system including its state, tote name, assigned sorter side, current/destination location, and state.. ontology_evidence.text: Model SortLocationsDatabaseModel (robotics): Contains all the sorter locations and their respective queue locations. The queue location is the location behind the sorter location where the AGV with an empty tote will move to fill when an exchange happens. Also a zone/shutdown-queue-sequence -> station/location mapping lookup used to translate a shutdown queue sequence number tied to a zone into the target sorter station/location.. nodes.purpose: Confirm that the hospital station accepts totes again and that the affected AGV and tote state no longer prevents normal flow.
nodes.diagnostic_reasoning: The source reports restoration of adding and removing totes and that all robots were re-added and running.

evidence_collection_procedures.title: Use RMS Map Monitor Message Panel to view AGV fault list, fault details, and locate a faulted AGV
evidence_collection_procedures.purpose: Use the RMS / fleet status UI Map Monitor message panel to identify faulted/disconnected AGVs, view the selected fault’s details, and use the “Locate Faulted AGV” control to bring up the corresponding location cue.

evidence_collection_procedures.title: WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) AGV state inspection
evidence_collection_procedures.purpose: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) live read-only database surface to inspect robotics-related AGV state records when the RMS / fleet status UI reports AGVs out of sync or the robotic system is stopped. nodes.title: Stop if hospital-state correction is unsupported or validation fails
nodes.intent: Hand off when the hospital tote or AGV state cannot be safely identified or the approved correction does not restore hospital tote flow.
nodes.goal: Hand off when the hospital tote or AGV state cannot be safely identified or the approved correction does not restore hospital tote flow.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to prepare an escalation handoff containing hospital HMI or layout evidence, AGV and tote association observations, API dog or Aveva action results, validation results, and clear stop criteria; the handoff procedure must identify the role authorized to continue.
nodes.source_supported_description: The packet documents uncertain cause, unreadable artifacts, and high-level state-correction actions without a complete supported procedure.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to prepare an escalation handoff containing hospital HMI or layout evidence, AGV and tote association observations, API dog or Aveva action results, validation results, and clear stop criteria; the handoff procedure must identify the role authorized to continue.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1/L2 support observes that the evidence is insufficient, the authorized interface cannot complete the supported correction, or hospital validation remains unsuccessful. Healthy signal for this gate is not recovery; it is a documented stop condition with sufficient evidence for the next role. Unhealthy continuation signal: further unapproved state changes, physical handling, or database changes would be required.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The packet contains an annotated hospital-area HMI-style layout used in the investigation.
The source describes using Aveva for AGV and tote state correction.

unhealthy_indicators: Supported correction cannot be completed or validated.
Further action would require unauthorized physical, database, or configuration changes.
inconclusive_indicators: The affected AGV, tote, or station cannot be uniquely identified.
Evidence is limited to second-hand reports or unreadable screenshots.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Do not treat the source's suspected removed-AGV explanation as confirmed diagnosis.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Incident summary states the exact cause was not known and lists several recovery actions.

nodes.primary_action: Stop and prepare an escalation handoff because the hospital state correction is unsupported, cannot be uniquely identified, or validation failed after the supported path.
nodes.performed_by: L2_support (required) with L1/L3 assistance to compile evidence and determine next authorized ownership
nodes.primary_surface: hospital_hmi + authorized interface evidence + site_interview summary (for handoff documentation)
evidence_to_collect: Hospital HMI/layout evidence showing add/induct status or inability to confirm
AGV and tote association observations from the diagnostic steps (unexpected placement, duplicate occupancy, orphaned association if known)
Results of attempted authorized correction (interface accepted/rejected; what changed or did not change)
Validation results (hospital add/induct succeeded/failed after correction)
nodes.healthy_interpretation: This node is not 'recovery'; it is a documented stop condition with sufficient evidence for the next role to continue safely.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Further unapproved state changes/physical/database actions would be required to proceed.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Evidence is limited to second-hand reports or unreadable screenshots such that the affected target cannot be uniquely identified.
nodes.generated_guidance: Do not treat the incident’s suspected 'removed-AGV explanation' as confirmed root cause. Escalate with a concise evidence bundle: what was observed at the hospital station, what backend/authorized interface states were found (as read-only evidence), what recovery attempts were executed, and what the hospital validation showed.

ontology_evidence.relevance: If the target mismatch cannot be uniquely identified or validation fails, the workflow must stop rather than continue with unapproved actions.

nodes.diagnostic_interpretation: Handoff is required whenever unique identification of the affected AGV/tote/state cannot be safely established or when hospital tote-flow validation fails.

structured_payload.title: Site cannot start or sustain sort
structured_payload.user_facing_summary: Troubleshoot a broad operational outage where the site cannot start sort or stops during sort, with possible server or service abnormality and subsequent recovery validation.
structured_payload.playbook_goal: Determine whether the report represents a site-wide sort availability problem, assess the source-supported service or server recovery direction, and validate stable operation without treating the historical service hypothesis as confirmed cause.
observed_entry_symptoms: The site goes down in the middle of sort.
Movement stops or the system is not running.
A work-order or repair note reports AGV hospital-station server issues and a need to reset services.
support_user_language_examples: We went down in the middle of sort
The site goes down in the middle of sort
Movement stops or the system is not running
A work-order or repair note reports AGV hospital-station
structured_payload.confidence_reason: The packet clearly documents site-down and sort-start failure reports, server/service-reset notes, a high-level OptiSweep service reset and Hospital Lane restart, and later reports that movement and the system resumed. Exact service diagnosis and validation evidence are incomplete.

nodes.title: Confirm site-wide sort unavailability
nodes.intent: Determine whether the report is a broad inability to start or sustain sort rather than only a localized hospital-station symptom.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the report is a broad inability to start or sustain sort rather than only a localized hospital-station symptom.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to confirm with the site whether sort is unavailable across the operation, whether movement stopped or only the hospital flow is affected, and whether the available site status or dashboard view shows a readable down or running state; do not infer the meaning of unreadable color cells.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source reports that the site was down and could not start sort or went down in the middle of sort; the associated dashboard screenshot is not readable enough to interpret independently.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to confirm with the site whether sort is unavailable across the operation, whether movement stopped or only the hospital flow is affected, and whether the available site status or dashboard view shows a readable down or running state; do not infer the meaning of unreadable color cells.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator reports whether sort cannot start or stopped during operation and whether movement is broadly affected; the source-evidenced status screenshot or site operational view is checked only for readable overall state. Healthy signal: sort starts and continues with normal movement. Unhealthy signal: site is down, sort cannot start, or sort stops broadly. Inconclusive: the screenshot is unreadable or the report is limited to one station or one AGV.

unhealthy_indicators: Site is reported down.

inconclusive_indicators: Only a localized hospital or AGV issue is reported.

evidence_to_collect: Site operator report: can sort start, and does it continue without stopping?
Site operator report: is movement absent across the operation, or are only hospital actions affected?

nodes.healthy_interpretation: Sort starts and continues with normal movement across the operation.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Site is down, sort cannot start, or sort stops broadly with movement absent.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Screenshot/artifact cannot be read; or reports only a localized hospital/AGV symptom that cannot be reproduced.
nodes.generated_guidance: Treat the unreadable dashboard as non-diagnostic. Use the operator’s ability to start/sustain sort and whether movement is broadly affected to determine whether this is a site-wide sort availability issue. Only then correlate with service evidence in the next node.
