nodes.title: Check for source-supported service or server abnormality
nodes.intent: Determine whether the broad outage correlates with the documented AGV hospital-station server or service abnormality.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the broad outage correlates with the documented AGV hospital-station server or service abnormality.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect the AGV hospital-station server or OptiSweep service state using the named service evidence available in the case, including Windows Services or Event Viewer only if the current diagnostic artifact identifies those views, and to distinguish a live service fault from a historical notes entry.
nodes.source_supported_description: The case artifacts and closure details mention AGV hospital-station server issues, services needing reset, and later reset of OptiSweep services, but do not show the live service state or exact service names.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect the AGV hospital-station server or OptiSweep service state using the named service evidence available in the case, including Windows Services or Event Viewer only if the current diagnostic artifact identifies those views, and to distinguish a live service fault from a historical notes entry.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1/L2 support inspects the documented service/server evidence and any available named service view. Healthy signal: relevant services are responsive and no abnormal condition is observed. Unhealthy signal: the named incident context continues to show a server or service abnormality, or service responsiveness is absent. Inconclusive: the packet provides only a notes entry saying services need reset and no live service state or exact service name is available.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The packet labels the AGV repair artifact as a Windows-services-related screenshot, although enrichment notes that the visible crop is a notes pane rather than a live Services console.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not identify exact OptiSweep service names or provide a validated event-log mapping.
The artifact is a notes pane rather than proof of a live Windows Services state.
healthy_indicators: Relevant service or server state is responsive.
No current service abnormality is observed in the available named view.
unhealthy_indicators: AGV hospital-station server is reported as having service issues.
OptiSweep services are reported as requiring reset or are not responsive.
inconclusive_indicators: Only a historical work-order note is available.
Exact service names and live state are unavailable.
The dashboard or service artifact cannot be read.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: AGV hospital station is described as having server issues and needing services reset.
Resolution details state that Opti sweep services were reset.

nodes.primary_action: Inspect the currently relevant evidence for the documented OptiSweep/AGV hospital-station server/service abnormality—confirm whether the services are currently responsive/healthy versus still abnormal—and distinguish live fault from historical notes-only evidence.
evidence_to_collect: Windows services / Event Viewer evidence for OptiSweep and any related WCSWebApplication failures or service restarts (confirm Running vs Stopped/abnormal patterns).
Whether the evidence corresponds to the time window of the sort outage (live/active vs only historical notes).

If service names are not visible in the artifact: collect what is available (the specific hosts/app names or the exact events shown in the current evidence artifact) so service mapping can be verified.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Relevant services are responsive/healthy; no abnormal server/service condition is present in current evidence.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Evidence shows continued service/server abnormality (services not running or crash/restart patterns) consistent with outage context.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Only a historical work-order note is available, with no exact service names or live service-state proof.

optional_corroboration.note: If service indicators are unclear, corroborate with current AGV/system error visibility using WCS-backed state (RMS/WCS evidence pairing) before concluding service fault.

linked_primary_procedure.title: Windows Event Viewer and Services diagnostic for OptiSweep and WCSWebApplication failures
linked_primary_procedure.purpose: Diagnose whether OptiSweep and WCSWebApplication failures map to service states (Running/Stopped) and relevant crash/restart events.
linked_primary_procedure.rationale: Node intent is to inspect the documented service/server abnormality; the top matching candidate is a specific Event Viewer/Services diagnostic for OptiSweep and WCSWebApplication failures. It matches the case enrichment that the artifact relates to Windows-services context (even if the visible crop may have been a notes pane).
match_gaps: Packet does not provide exact service names; procedure must be able to identify them from event/log context once opened.

nodes.generated_guidance: Do not assume that 'services need reset' from a work-order note is still the live fault. Confirm current evidence: service running state and any crash/restart patterns. If you cannot identify the affected services from the artifact, record a catalog/working-set gap and proceed to escalation per gate logic.

nodes.purpose: Determine whether the broad outage correlates with the documented AGV hospital-station server or service abnormality.
nodes.diagnostic_reasoning: The case artifacts and closure details mention AGV hospital-station server issues, services needing reset, and later reset of OptiSweep services, but do not show the live service state or exact service names.

evidence_collection_procedures.title: Windows Event Viewer and Services diagnostic for OptiSweep and WCSWebApplication failures
evidence_collection_procedures.purpose: Use Windows Event Viewer / services to inspect the live Windows Application and System logs, then verify the current OptiSweep service state. Correlate WCSWebApplication database-command errors around 6:35-6:36 AM with OptiSweep Service Control Manager Event 7031 and the current Windows Services status before further recovery.

evidence_collection_procedures.title: WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) AGV state inspection
evidence_collection_procedures.purpose: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) live read-only database surface to inspect robotics-related AGV state records when the RMS / fleet status UI reports AGVs out of sync or the robotic system is stopped. Compare the populated SSMS State results with the live RMS / fleet status UI; the listed state values do not independently establish a fault.

fields.name: IsToteEmpty

fields.name: ToteId
fields.meaning: Tote currently associated with robot (labeled ToteId in the live query results

fields.name: CommandId
fields.meaning: FK to the robot's current RobotCommandDatabaseModel row

fields.name: Coordinate
fields.meaning: Location label for the robot's coordinate reference (observed value "RoboticsModule.Messages.Location")

fields.name: Current
fields.meaning: Live electrical current draw reported by the AGV

fields.name: State
fields.meaning: Robot state enum (Tipper/Hospital/Charger/Sorter/GLD/ShutDown family). Observed live values include SWaitingInzone, Removed, SWaitingForExchange, GoCharge, MovingToChargerEntranceQueue, MovingToTipperQueue

fields.name: CellCode
fields.meaning: Current cell/lattice code the robot is reporting (cross-references CellCodeDatabaseModel.CellCode)

fields.name: ChargeKick
fields.meaning: Whether the robot was kicked off the charger (relates to ChargingThresholdsDatabaseModel kick-off threshold)

nodes.question: Determine whether the broad outage correlates with the documented AGV hospital-station server or service abnormality.

runbook_execution_result.success: Windows Event Viewer / services inspection identifies whether current Application log evidence includes WCSWebApplication Event ID 20102 or clustered related errors.
runbook_execution_result.failure: WCSWebApplication Event ID 20102 or clustered application errors are present or repeating in the current inspection.

node_interpretation_mapping.success: Relevant services responsive; no live server/service abnormality observed.
node_interpretation_mapping.failure: Live service/server abnormality indicated (continued failure or unresponsive services).
node_interpretation_mapping.inconclusive: Insufficient live evidence; only historical notes exist or service mapping is missing.

nodes.title: Perform authorized service or lane recovery
nodes.intent: Use the approved procedure for the documented service or Hospital Lane recovery path when the responsible role confirms that it is authorized and supported.
nodes.goal: Use the approved procedure for the documented service or Hospital Lane recovery path when the responsible role confirms that it is authorized and supported.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed for authorized recovery of the source-named OptiSweep services and Hospital Lane, including operational safety preconditions, role limits, service-state evidence, and post-recovery checks; exact restart steps and commands belong in the runbook.
nodes.source_supported_description: The closure summary says OptiSweep services were reset and the site restarted Hospital Lane; the packet does not provide exact steps.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed for authorized recovery of the source-named OptiSweep services and Hospital Lane, including operational safety preconditions, role limits, service-state evidence, and post-recovery checks; exact restart steps and commands belong in the runbook.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1/L2 support or the authorized site role observes that the approved service recovery or Hospital Lane restart has completed. Progress signal: service responsiveness or lane availability returns. Unhealthy signal: the recovery is rejected, the service remains abnormal, or the action would affect an unsafe or unknown operational state. Inconclusive: completion is asserted but no observable service, lane, or movement change is available.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Closure details state that the site restarted Hospital Lane; hospital station and Hospital Lane are named in the incident.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not provide exact service names, restart sequence, or a validated Hospital Lane control mapping.
healthy_indicators: Authorized recovery is completed.
Service or Hospital Lane responsiveness returns.
Movement begins again.
unhealthy_indicators: Service remains unavailable or the lane does not recover.
Recovery causes or reveals additional AGV, tote, or safety anomalies.
inconclusive_indicators: Recovery completion is reported without a direct operational observation.
No authorized role is available to perform the supported recovery.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Do not infer that resetting services is safe or sufficient without the approved procedure and role authorization.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Reset Opti sweep services and had site restart Hospital Lane.

nodes.primary_action: Perform the authorized recovery for the documented OptiSweep services and restart Hospital Lane only after confirming authorization and supported preconditions; then observe for lane/service responsiveness returning.
evidence_to_collect: Authorization confirmation from the responsible role to perform the recovery action.
Service/lane recovery completion evidence available to the performing role (e.g., lane availability and responsiveness).
Post-recovery operational observation: movement begins again; hospital lane availability restored.
Any new anomalies revealed during recovery (AGV/tote/safety) for triage.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Authorized recovery is completed and Hospital Lane/service responsiveness returns; movement begins again.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Recovery is rejected, service/lane remains unavailable, or action would create/affect an unsafe/unknown operational state.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Completion is asserted without direct operational observation, or no authorized role is available to perform recovery.

linked_primary_procedure.title: Recover hospital tote flow using Apidog / WCS API and validate AGV operation
linked_primary_procedure.purpose: Execute a supported recovery path for the documented hospital lane/tote flow and validate AGV operation after recovery.
linked_primary_procedure.rationale: A case-local incident-derived recovery procedure is present and is conceptually closest to 'Hospital Lane restart' and service recovery validation, but the node’s procedure placeholder is explicitly about OptiSweep services + Hospital Lane recovery; the candidate is hospital tote flow recovery via API rather than a generic lane restart. This must be SME-reviewed for fit.
match_gaps: Procedure may not include the documented 'OptiSweep services reset + Hospital Lane restart' exact sequence for this specific outage.
Packet does not include exact lane control mapping; node requires authorization and safety preconditions that may not align to this API-focused candidate.

nodes.generated_guidance: Only perform actions after confirming authorization and supported operational preconditions. After completion, confirm lane availability and movement restoration before proceeding to validation; do not declare success based only on claimed restart completion.

ontology_evidence.evidence_summary: Defines hospital diversion/lane routing recovery verification patterns; supports using hospital lane responsiveness and movement restoration as the expected outcome.

nodes.diagnostic_interpretation: Execute the responsible, authorized recovery path when service abnormality is confirmed and authorization is available.

evidence_collection_procedures.title: Recover hospital tote flow using Apidog / WCS API and validate AGV operation
evidence_collection_procedures.purpose: For the UPS Haslet TX (TXRTH) hospital-station tote-induction condition, use the Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU to pause the station when operators are not present at the tippers, then use Apidog / WCS API to remove the inducted or disconnected tote state and recover affected AGV state. Validate tote add/remove operation on the Hospital HMI / lane UI, confirm affected robots are re-added and operating, and confirm the system is running. The incident did not establish a single definitive root cause or provide exact API request names, parameters, or AGV control names.

nodes.title: Validate stable sort and movement recovery
nodes.intent: Confirm that the site can start or sustain sort and that movement remains active after service or lane recovery.
nodes.goal: Confirm that the site can start or sustain sort and that movement remains active after service or lane recovery.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to validate OptiSweep or service responsiveness, confirm Hospital Lane and site sort operation, observe sustained movement, and check for recurrence after recovery; the validation procedure should define the monitoring interval and evidence to retain without prescribing exact screen navigation.
nodes.source_supported_description: The packet reports that movement started and the system was running, while the earlier symptom was inability to start or sustain sort.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to validate OptiSweep or service responsiveness, confirm Hospital Lane and site sort operation, observe sustained movement, and check for recurrence after recovery; the validation procedure should define the monitoring interval and evidence to retain without prescribing exact screen navigation.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator observes sort startup and continued movement, while support verifies any available named service or operational status view. Healthy signal: sort starts, movement is active, and the site remains running. Unhealthy signal: sort cannot start, the site goes down again, or movement stops. Inconclusive: a general message says the system is running but no sustained sort or movement observation is available.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Teams messages report that movement started and that the system was running.
The resolution path names Hospital Lane as part of recovery.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology does not provide a detailed mapping for sustained sort validation or the specific Hospital Lane status.
healthy_indicators: Site reports sort started successfully.
Movement is occurring and remains active.
System is reported running after recovery.
unhealthy_indicators: Sort cannot start.
Sort stops again after recovery.
Movement does not resume or quickly stops.
inconclusive_indicators: Only a single 'system is running' message is available.
No direct observation of sustained sort or movement is available.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: If broad sort availability is not restored or stability cannot be demonstrated, use the escalation gate rather than declaring recovery.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Chat reports that movement started and the system was running.

nodes.primary_action: Validate sustained sort and movement recovery after the service/lane recovery phase, including confirming continued operation (no quick recurrence) over a monitoring interval.
evidence_to_collect: Operator observation that sort started and remains active (no immediate stop/second outage).
Operator observation that movement is occurring and remains active during the monitoring interval.
Support corroboration from an available operational status view (if any) and/or WCS/OptiSweep-related state evidence when accessible.
Any recurrence signals (sort stops again or site goes down again).
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Sort starts and remains active; movement is active; system remains running after recovery.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Sort cannot start, stops again, or movement does not resume / quickly stops.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Only a general 'system is running' message is available; insufficient direct observation of sustained sort/movement.

optional_corroboration.note: For system-state corroboration after a state-changing action, verify WCS/SSMS-backed state in parallel when available (do not rely on a single conversational 'running' message).

nodes.generated_guidance: Validation is not a one-time claim. Establish a monitoring interval and ensure continued evidence collection supports sustained recovery. If sustained behavior is not demonstrated, do not proceed—use the escalation gate.

ontology_evidence.title: WCS model — CellCodeDatabaseModel

source_refs.note: PascalCase model inventory

ontology_evidence.text: Model CellCodeDatabaseModel (robotics): Stores all cell codes in the map. When a new AGV is added to the system while in a running state, the system first checks if the AGV's current cell code is in a missing zone under the sorter; if not, it uses this table to look up which hospital the cell code is connected to and sends an Initialize command to Geek.. Fields: CellCode: Cell/node code analogous to an RMS node code (vendor-agnostic).; X: X coordinate for the cell code.; Y: Y coordinate for the

ontology_evidence.title: WCS model — HospitalTagsModel

source_refs.note: PascalCase model inventory; live query screenshot on p.93 supplied real column names (TagTypeParent/TagTypeChild/TagPath/VariableType/StringValue/IntValue/UintValue/BoolValue/Date_Time/HospitalStationId), resolving the prior needs_sme value-column-mechanism gap

ontology_evidence.text: Model HospitalTagsModel (sorter_sweeper): List of tags subscribed to for processing data from the hospital controller; the system takes action based on TagTypeParent (in/out).. Fields: Id: Row id.; EntityInserted: Insert timestamp.; EntityLastUpdate: Last update timestamp.; TagTypeParent: Whether the tag is in or out; drives which action the system takes, e.g. stConfirmBtn1_1, stExtract, stReinductToteBtn1_5, stRemoveToteBtn1_6, sInduct, sRFID_READ, CallMaintBtn1_7.; TagTypeChild: Sub-type/child

ontology_evidence.text: Model RobotDatabaseModel (robotics): Robot/AGV live state: contains the data for every robot in the system including its state, tote name, assigned sorter side, current/destination location, and state.. Fields: Name: Robot code / AGV identifier (e.g. 1555058).; State: Robot state enum (Tipper/Hospital/Charger/Sorter/GLD/ShutDown family). fields.name: IsToteEmpty
fields.meaning: Whether the tote currently on the robot is empty (1) or not (0).

fields.name: ChargeKick

source_refs.note: PascalCase model inventory; live query screenshot on p.77 supplied the full column list and example values

fields.name: VariableType
fields.meaning: Selects which typed value column is active for this row (BoolVal, StringVal, IntVal, UintVal); this is the modular "variable type" mechanism — the lookup selects the value column, and only that column is populated while the others stay NULL.

fields.name: TagTypeParent
fields.meaning: Whether the tag is in or out; drives which action the system takes, e.g. stConfirmBtn1_1, stExtract, stReinductToteBtn1_5, stRemoveToteBtn1_6, sInduct, sRFID_READ, CallMaintBtn1_7.

fields.name: BoolValue
fields.meaning: Active value when VariableType selects the bool column, e.g. 0/1/2; NULL otherwise.

source_refs.note: PascalCase model inventory; live query screenshot on p.93 supplied real column names (TagTypeParent/TagTypeChild/TagPath/VariableType/StringValue/IntValue/UintValue/BoolValue/Date_Time/HospitalStationId), resolving the prior needs_sme value-column-mechanism gap

fields.name: In-progress time
fields.meaning: Lifecycle timestamp/indicator: when the command transitioned to in-progress. Until a command is marked in-progress, the current destination location's queue/capacity remains held; once in-progress, that queue/location capacity is freed up. A row present with a sent time but no in-progress time (not progressing) indicates a stuck command.

fields.name: Sent time
fields.meaning: Lifecycle timestamp: when the command was sent. Present before the command is marked in-progress.

fields.name: Command status
fields.meaning: Status of the command.

nodes.intent: Hand off when the service or server condition cannot be confirmed, authorized recovery does not restore operation, or the site remains unable to start or sustain sort.

nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to prepare escalation evidence including service or server observations, Event Viewer or Windows Services evidence when available, sort availability reports, Hospital Lane state, recovery actions attempted, and validation results, with stop criteria and the receiving technical role.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source contains incomplete service evidence, an unreadable dashboard artifact, and a site-wide outage that eventually recovered through multiple actions.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to prepare escalation evidence including service or server observations, Event Viewer or Windows Services evidence when available, sort availability reports, Hospital Lane state, recovery actions attempted, and validation results, with stop criteria and the receiving technical role.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1/L2 support observes unresolved service abnormality, failed recovery, repeated outage, or insufficient evidence to continue safely. Healthy signal for this gate is a complete evidence package and controlled handoff, not continued troubleshooting. Unhealthy continuation signal: repeated resets, unsupported changes, or declaring recovery from a single unverified status message.

healthy_indicators: Evidence package complete and controlled handoff prepared.
unhealthy_indicators: Sort remains unavailable after the supported recovery path.
The site repeatedly goes down or cannot start sort.
Further recovery would require unsupported or unauthorized changes.
inconclusive_indicators: Only an unreadable dashboard or historical notes entry is available.
The service name or current state cannot be identified.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Historical unfamiliarity, support participation, and communication delays are not themselves escalation conditions; escalation is based on unsafe, unsupported, or unresolved technical state.

nodes.primary_action: Prepare an evidence package for controlled handoff/escalation when service recovery or sustained sort validation fails or cannot be confirmed; stop further unsupported recovery attempts.
evidence_to_collect: What remains unresolved: service/server abnormality, lane recovery failure, or sort unavailability after validation attempt.
Service or server evidence when available (Event Viewer/service state screenshots or event IDs).
Sort availability reports (site interview confirmations and any operational observations).
Hospital Lane state/recovery actions attempted (including who performed what, and when).
Validation results and whether recurrence was observed.
A clear statement of evidence gaps (missing service names/live state, unreadable dashboard, or inability to reproduce).
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Evidence indicates unresolved abnormal state or repeated outages; further recovery would require unsupported/unauthorized changes.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Only unreadable dashboard or historical notes exist and the service/current state cannot be identified.
nodes.generated_guidance: Escalation here is evidence-driven: provide the receiving technical role a complete package and stop criteria. Historical ambiguity or communication delays alone are not sufficient—evidence gaps must be explicitly listed.

ontology_evidence.evidence_summary: Supports the idea that escalation requires evidence of service abnormality/crash/restart evidence rather than assumptions.

nodes.escalation_reason: Hand off when the service or server condition cannot be confirmed, authorized recovery does not restore operation, or the site remains unable to start or sustain sort.
evidence_package: What remains unresolved: service/server abnormality, lane recovery failure, or sort unavailability after validation attempt.
Service or server evidence when available (Event Viewer/service state screenshots or event IDs).
Sort availability reports (site interview confirmations and any operational observations).
Hospital Lane state/recovery actions attempted (including who performed what, and when).
Validation results and whether recurrence was observed.
A clear statement of evidence gaps (missing service names/live state, unreadable dashboard, or inability to reproduce).
